messages.text: Will a power spike fry the whole miner?

Great question — this is actually one of the things the Rev 6.1 specifically addresses.

**There's an onboard F1 fuse built right into the board**, sitting beside the yellow XT30 power input. It's a sacrificial automotive-style blade fuse — if a power spike hits, **F1 blows first**, taking the hit so the rest of the electronics don't.

The short version:
- Spike comes in → F1 fuse goes → miner's guts survive
- Replace a $0.50 fuse, not a $249 miner
- Cheaper units skip this entirely — a spike there cooks everything behind it

**Also helping:** the included **350 W MEANWELL PSU** is a proper industrial supply, not a cheap brick — it's far more stable under load than the budget adapters competitors bundle.

So no, a spike isn't a "goodbye miner" moment here the way it can be on lesser boards. 👍
What stops it from overheating or dying?

Good one — the Rev 6.1 has a few layers working together on this:

**1. Spring-mounted heatsink + front fan**
The spring presses evenly on all four BM1370 chips — no one "hot corner" die cooking faster than the rest. Result: **~57 °C at full 6 TH/s**, ~40–45 dB. Desk-friendly, not garage-loud.

**2. Custom BSB airflow shroud**
Most boards leave the voltage regulators (VRMs) completely bare — they're the part that typically dies first. BSB's shroud ducts the fan's cold air **directly onto the VRMs**. Result: **VRM temps ~54 °C at full load** — the usual first-to-fail part is the one they cooled.

**3. XT30 connector + thicker PCB**
The R. 5 used an 8 A barrel jack that sagged and melted under load. Rev 6.1 swaps in a **15 A XT30 connector** + thicker copper PCB — so the power path itself doesn't become a heat source.

**4. The onboard F1 fuse**
As covered — takes a spike so the electronics don't have to.

**5. Oversized MEANWELL PSU**
Loafing at ~30% of its 350 W cap····feeding a ~100 W miner — a cool, stable supply puts far less stress on the whole system than a maxed-out cheap brick.

It's not one thing — it's all five working together for 24/7 reliability.
Is the included power supply actually reliable?

Yes — and it's not a close call.

The included **MEANWELL LRS-350-12** is a proper industrial power supply:
- **350 W / 29 A cap····** feeding a miner that draws **~100 W at full speed**
- That's loafing at roughly **~30% of its rated load** — cool, quiet, long-lived
- **UL / CE / UKCA certified** — not a no-name brick

**Why that matters:**
Cheap competitors bundle ~99–124 W adapters into miners that pull ~100 W — those are running flat-out 24/7, which is exactly how PSUs fail early. And when a cheap brick fails under load, it can take the miner with it.

**The headroom proof:** the same MEANWELL LRS-350-12 was used in overclock research that pushed a NerdQaxe++ to **10 TH/s** (extreme custom-cooled lab run — not a stock claim). The P. handled it fine.

Bottom line: it's an industrial supply rated for way more than this miner needs, certified, and ships **included in the box** — unbox, plug in, run. No sourcing a separate PSU.
